title: Edit-revision MUST push contradicts retention permission
description:
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md
Lines: 973 (vs context at 546)

Current state — line 546 already permits servers to limit retained revisions:
  "Servers MAY limit the number of retained revisions; if so, older revisions MAY be elided."

But the edit procedure at line 973 still mandates a per-edit push:
  "Push a MessageRevision onto editHistory with the current body, bodyType, and current server time as editedAt."

A privacy-focused deployment may legitimately want to retain zero edit history (the `editedAt` flag alone tells clients an edit occurred; the prior text is gone). As written, the spec straddles: line 546 permits retention limits but line 973 mandates each individual revision push.

Two viable fixes (pick one):

Option A — soften line 973 step 1:
  "If the server retains edit history, push a MessageRevision onto editHistory with the current body, bodyType, and current server time as editedAt."

Option B — amend line 546 to be explicit about zero retention:
  "Servers MAY limit the number of retained revisions, including to zero; if so, older revisions MAY be elided."

Option A is cleaner because it removes the MUST contradiction at the point of action; Option B leaves the procedural MUST intact and reinterprets it via the retention paragraph. Recommend Option A.
acceptance_criteria:
- Line 973 step 1 does not contradict line 546
- A zero-retention deployment is unambiguously permitted by the spec text
- The editedAt-flag-set behavior on edits is retained unchanged
- No change to clients' observability of `editedAt` (which is set regardless of retention)
